ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the rectangle $ABCD$ is folded along the line $AE$, with the vertex $D$ precisely landing on point $F$ on side $BC$. Given that $CE=3\,\text{cm}$ and $AB=8\,\text{cm}$, what is the area of the shaded section?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the properties of folding, $EF=DE=CD-CE=5$, $AD=AF=BC$,\\
by the Pythagorean theorem, $CF=4$, $AF^2=AB^2+BF^2$,\\
thus $AD^2=8^2+(AD-4)^2$,\\
Solving gives, $AD=10$,\\
$\therefore BF=6$,\\
The area of the shaded part in the diagram is $S_{\triangle ABF}+S_{\triangle CEF}=\boxed{30\text{cm}^2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; point E is on the right side CD, and point F is on the bottom side BC. The dashed line shows the crease AE and the AF and EF formed after folding, and the shaded part consists of the left triangle ABF and the right triangle CEF. Reasoning: Let the horizontal side of the rectangle be AD=BC=x. Because AB=CD=8 cm, and CE=3 cm, DE=CD-CE=8-3=5 cm. By the property of folding, D lands on F, and the points A and E on the crease AE remain fixed, so EF=DE=5 cm, AF=AD=x. In right triangle CEF, CE=3 cm and EF=5 cm, so CF=sqrt(5^2-3^2)=4 cm. Therefore BF=BC-CF=x-4. In right triangle ABF, AF^2=AB^2+BF^2, so x^2=8^2+(x-4)^2. Solving gives x=10, therefore BF=10-4=6 cm. The shaded area is the area of triangle ABF plus the area of triangle CEF: 1/2×8×6 + 1/2×3×4 = 24+6 = 30 cm².
